newsitem.title: FRANCE: McDonald's launches hamburger "for French tastes".
newsitem.headline: McDonald's launches hamburger "for French tastes".

text.p: McDonald's Corp., which already makes 7 billion francs ($1.2 billion) a year in France, is launching a new hamburger specially aimed at Gallic tastes, the fast-food giant said Thursday.
The "Mc Deluxe," which goes on sale Friday, will attempt to do away with the slightly sweet-and-sour taste given traditional McDonald's hamburgers by ketchup.
Ketchup will be replaced by a new sauce composed of pepper and traditional French mustard, giving the product a more salty and spicy taste, a spokeswoman said.

The French public's increasing desire for healthier foods will also see a thicker tomato slice and a full, non-shredded lettuce leaf inserted into the "Mc Deluxe," together with onions and a slice of cheddar cheese, a spokeswoman said.

McDonald's is France's biggest fast-food chain with some 500 outlets. The new product is aimed at people over 35 and at women who, according to market studies, are wary of ketchup. Another target is youths aged 12-14 who do not eat ketchup in French homes and may also be adverse to it.
The name "Mc Deluxe" already applies to other McDonald's products sold elsewhere in the world but will only apply to the "French-taste" hamburger when sold in France.
